clauses.reason: Blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Haiti and the de facto regime, and entities they own or control, notwithstanding international agreements and prior contracts or licenses. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Blocks property of any Haitian national providing substantial financial or material contributions to, or doing substantial business with, the de facto regime, as identified by the Secretary of the Treasury. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Lead of Sec. 3: introduces the prohibitions in items (a) to (c). Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits sale or supply of petroleum, petroleum products, arms and related materiel to Haiti or for business there, and activities promoting such sale or supply. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits carriage on U.S.-registered vessels of petroleum, petroleum products or arms and related materiel with entry into or intent to enter Haiti's territory (the held text spans a page break inside this item). Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits transactions that evade or avoid, or attempt to violate, the prohibitions. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Withdraws the section 2(c)(iii) food exemption of EO 12779 for exportations in which the regime or an identified person is a party. Later event: EO 12917 (signed 1994-05-21) Sec. 4 revokes section 4 of EO 12853 to the extent inconsistent with EO 12917, effective 11:59 p.m. EDT May 21, 1994 and only for later actions; EO 12917 Sec. 1(d) re-sets the export prohibition and its exemptions in its own terms, so the revocation is partial and conditional and the clause continues until EO 12932. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Defines Haitian national and incorporates the section 3 definitions of EO 12779. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of State, to issue regulations under IEEPA and the United Nations Participation Act, including on entry of vessels and aircraft, and directs agencies to cooperate. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Revokes section 4 of EO 12775 and sections 2(c) and 4 of EO 12779 to the extent inconsistent, and provides that this order supplements EO 12779 otherwise. A conditional partial revocation of other orders persists as long as the inconsistency, so it runs with this order; it is a performed amendment of those orders, which EO 12932 later revokes outright. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

States that the order creates no right or benefit enforceable against the United States. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.
States that the order is effective immediately, which fixes its effectiveness at signing, June 30, 1993. An effective-date provision is spent when the stated time arrives, 1993-06-30.

Directs transmittal to the Congress and publication in the Federal Register. The Federal Register text does not show when, or whether, the Congress transmittal was made, so no earlier performance date is established; the clause runs with the order. EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The dossier flags that the sources read as both a whole and a partial ending for EO 12932. Resolution: EO 12932 revokes this order by number in a single sentence that names eight orders and also terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775, so it is a whole ending. Earlier partial provisions held for some of these orders (revocations to the extent inconsistent in later Haiti orders) are recorded as later events of the clauses they touch; each is conditional on inconsistency and none is shown to extinguish a clause, so none is an end.

research_rationale:
EO 12853 of June 30, 1993 (Blocking Government of Haiti Property and Prohibiting Transactions With Haiti), read in full in the held Federal Register text (58 FR 35843, Federal Register of July 2, 1993; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1993-06-30). The order blocks the Haitian Government's and the regime's property, blocks property of identified Haitian nationals, prohibits petroleum and arms trade, withdraws part of an export exemption, defines terms, authorizes Treasury regulations, and partially revokes earlier Haiti orders. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory stops after Sec. 3(b) and mis-numbers Sec. 3 items as Sec. 2, omitting Sec. 3(c) and Sec. 4 to Sec. 8; I re-marked thirteen clauses on the held text. EO 12917 revokes Sec. 4 to the extent inconsistent (later event). EO 12932 revokes the order by number effective 12:01 a.m. EDT October 16, 1994. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 10. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number include EO 12917 (which names its section 4) and EO 12932.

savings.reason: EO 12932 states that the termination of the national emergency does not affect any action taken or proceeding pending, any action or proceeding based on an act committed before its effective date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties incurred before it. Those preserved effects, and any Treasury regulations or licenses issued under the order, are accrued consequences or separate administrative acts; they are not commands of this order. No held source shows an independent standing command of this order after 1994-10-16.
